findings.reason: without the invocation clause the node's constructed snapshot silently reproduces the dead control the section was rewritten to replace, and the recorded control reads "did not fire" for a reason that is a property of the fixture rather than of the derivation.
findings.text: §8's second control depends on the waiting plan's followup being attributed to a section, which requires its prompt to carry a `/reckon-<verb> <target> §N` invocation naming the section that declares the edge; the text says only that the prompt "names that edge's target section". Measured on this tree through `roadmap.build_roadmap`: a followup whose prompt is "waits for o#s3 to land" with no invocation produces 0 `undeclared-wait` findings both before and after the edge is removed (control dead); an invocation naming the declaring section produces 0 when declared and 1 when removed (the intended arm); an invocation naming a different section produces 1 in both states (false positive at the declared arm)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the changed text adds no href; its one citation is §2, and §2's landing comment (line 276) records the three-plan power_convertor critical path that §8 now compares against.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's second control names a followup whose *prompt* names the removed edge's target section, but `undeclared-wait` only ever reads a followup's mention when the followup carries a parseable `/reckon-<verb> <target> §N` invocation whose section is the declaring section, so a snapshot built exactly as written leaves that control unable to fire.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the changed text moves the control snapshot onto a committed builder under `tests/`, so a later reader can rebuild it and re-run both arms, and the results still go to the cumulative landed record.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed text introduces no symbol, file or comment that carries a plan, stage or ticket label; "§2" is a plan cross-reference in plan prose, not a code name.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the section no longer claims the base disagrees with today's coordinators (the 2026-11-06 re-measure at line 363 records that it did not), it dates the premise to the 2026-11-06 snapshots, and it scopes the controls to a constructed snapshot, so each stated mechanism now produces the measure the section asserts.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 asks for one thing, the four coordinator questions re-asked through the new reads on three mounts, with the two controls measuring that one deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §8's `plan-section-depends-on` entry (s2, s3, s4, s5, s7, s15, s16 plus `a-coordinator-sees-the-board#s13` and `the-mcp-answers-the-question-asked#s11`) names nodes that exist; the §8 landing comments record why the two cross-plan waits were added, and the changed text adds no edge it does not need.
